title: Taskgrind: Heavyweight Dynamic Binary Instrumentation for Parallel Programs Analysis
problem: Determinacy races are concurrent programming hazards where two accesses to the same memory address are not properly ordered with at least one being a write, indicating potential correctness errors in task-based parallel programs using models like Cilk and OpenMP.
motivation: Detecting and helping programmers fix determinacy races is critical for ensuring correctness in parallel programs before deployment.
method: The tool builds on Valgrind (a program inspection framework) by adding heavyweight monitoring that watches every instruction as the program actually runs—it's thorough but slows things down considerably. It records every memory access made by concurrent tasks (pieces of work running in parallel) and flags races: situations where two accesses to the same memory location aren't properly ordered and at least one is writing. Because it understands how Cilk and OpenMP organize parallel work, it avoids many false alarms that simpler tools raise, catching actual problems without noise.
key_novelty: By combining detailed runtime monitoring (watching every memory access) with awareness of parallel programming models, it detects races in Cilk and OpenMP programs that simpler tools miss.
contributions: Taskgrind tool for memory access analysis in parallel programming models like Cilk and OpenMP
Determinacy race detection with fewer false negatives than state-of-the-art tools
Reduced memory instrumentation overhead compared to competing approaches
Practical error reports to assist programmers during parallelization
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract provided.
primary_theme: Detecting concurrency bugs in parallel programs
